transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sofia R., Ethan C., Priya N. — Maya C., Oliver P., Ravi S., Tanya L.

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming behavior, parameter tuning (temp/top_p/max_tokens/stop), retry/timeout patterns and graceful failover. Walked customer through console sandbox and Optimize recommendations for batching/caching. Agreed on next steps: send pricing, sandbox invite, and schedule infra deep dive.

Topics covered:
- Streaming mechanics and client behavior (incremental deltas, content-type streaming)
- Idempotency, request keys, and safe retries/backoff
- Parameters: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, frequency/presence penalties, stop tokens
- Retry strategies for transient errors vs permanent errors, exponential backoff, jitter, circuit breaker basics
- Console tour: live streams, token usage, per-route latency breakdowns
- Redwood Optimize hints: prefix caching, auto-batching windows, quantization recommendations for cost savings
- Security/Compliance notes: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, data retention, VPC/private options

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia R: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro — I'm Sofia, AE on the Redwood hosted team. We got Ethan who will demo the API and Priya to show a quick console snippet.
[00:12] Maya C: Hi - thanks, excited. We wanted to see the streaming behavior and how retries work. Performance is a big one for us.
[00:18] Ethan C: Great. I'll start with a simple chat request. We'll show standard params and then streaming so you can see partial tokens arriving.
[00:25] Oliver P: Quick context — Lantern runs chat as part of messages in-app, typical request size ~150 tokens, target p95 < 400ms, and we expect bursts up to 200 rps.
[00:40] Ethan C: Okay noted. So first, synchronous call would return full text; streaming gives you chunks — partial deltas — which lets you show typing UI faster. Here, temp=0.2, max_tokens=200, stop=['\n\n'] — you'll see it stream.
[01:05] [stream starts] Speaker 1: "Hello — thanks for reaching out, I'm looking into that now..." (partial chunks)
[01:18] Maya C: Looks like partials arrive quickly. If we have lots of concurrent streams, does that increase latency?
[01:25] Ethan C: Good question. Per-request latency is mostly kernel and queueing. Higher concurrency can increase queuing, which is where batching helps for throughput but may add a tiny bit to tail latency. Redwood Optimize suggests small batching windows for low-latency use cases.
[01:45] Priya N: In the console I'll show you the per-route histogram so you can see p50/p95/p99; you can configure autoscale and burst capacity there.
[01:55] Ravi S: On retries — what do you recommend? Our network sometimes returns 504s under brief load spikes.
[02:02] Ethan C: We tend to recommend idempotency keys for mutating flows; for plain generation, treat 5xx as transient: do exponential backoff with jitter, e.g. base 200ms, factor 2, max backoff ~5s, cap retries to 3. Avoid immediate tight retries which amplify load. Also, if you see 429, consider softer client-side throttling and fallback to smaller model variant.
[02:30] Oliver P: Does the SDK handle idempotency automatically?
[02:35] Priya N: Our SDK exposes request_id and idempotency_key helpers; we won't retry if the response contains model-level errors like invalid tokenization.
[02:45] Maya C: Walk us through parameters — temperature vs top_p — which should we tune first?
[02:52] Ethan C: Temperature affects randomness directly; top_p does nucleus sampling. For most deterministic assistant flows we run temp 0 to 0.3 and top_p 0.9-1.0. If you're doing more exploratory creative text, increase temp. Also watch max_tokens as that drives cost directly. Use stop tokens to avoid runaway outputs.
[03:20] Tanya L: We sometimes need structured outputs (JSON). How do you ensure model doesn't hallucinate fields?
[03:25] Ethan C: Two tactics: use function/tool calling for strict structured outputs, or provide strict pattern instructions + sampling settings low temp. Also Redwood Optimize can run evals against prompt sets and flag regressions if JSON fields break — we can automate monitoring.
[03:45] Maya C: About fallbacks — you mentioned smaller model variant — how transparent is that?
[03:50] Sofia R: Smart routing can fallback to a compatible variant (e.g., 8B quantized) when the primary is at capacity. It’s policy-driven: you can set latency-first or cost-first. We surface metrics so you know when fallbacks kicked in.
[04:10] Ravi S: For our security team — do you support SSO and audit logs? Data at rest encryption?
[04:15] Sofia R: Yes: SSO (SAML/SSO) + RBAC, audit logs available in Console, KMS-backed encryption for private deployments, and SOC 2 compliance. We can also discuss VPC private control plane options if needed.
[04:40] Oliver P: Cost concerns — how do we estimate tokens and keep costs predictable?
[04:45] Priya N: Console shows token breakdown by prompt/response and per-route cost. Optimize will suggest quantization or batching to reduce unit cost. We also provide committed Dedicated capacity if you want predictable monthly billing.
[05:05] Ethan C: Quick demo of retries in practice: we'll simulate a transient 503 and show client backoff. Note the SDK wraps responses so you can capture partial deltas and rehydrate the stream on retry — but be careful about duplicate tokens; we provide token offsets to make merging easier.
[05:35] [Demo: simulated 503 -> backoff -> retry] Speaker 2: "...attempting retry 1 after 350ms jitter..."
[06:05] Maya C: That looked smooth. For our mobile clients we need idempotency and short timeouts — any best practice?
[06:12] Ethan C: Use shorter client-side timeouts for interactive flows (e.g., 1–2s for initial stanza), stream partials aggressively, and provide graceful degrade UX. For mobile you might fallback to cached response or summary when latency is high.
[06:40] Tanya L: Console tour?
[06:42] Priya N: Switching over now — here's the sandbox project, you can see a live stream session, token counts, and the optimize panel which highlights prefix cacheable prompts and suggests batching window of 10–30ms for Lantern's profile.
[07:05] [screen share noise / brief silence]
[07:20] Oliver P: That optimize hint — what is prefix caching?
[07:23] Ethan C: If you have repeated system prompts or shared history fragments, Redwood caches the KV cache prefix so subsequent requests reuse the cached key/value and skip recomputation, saving tokens and compute. It's transparent and works per-tenant with configurable TTL.
[07:45] Maya C: Any limitations for PII? We hold some user transcripts that might be sensitive.
[07:50] Sofia R: For PII we recommend Private deployment or VPC options; hosted customers can opt into short retention windows and enterprise contracts with data handling addenda. We also do per-customer keying for some features.
[08:10] Ravi S: For our scale, what about batching? We worry that batching could hurt tail latency.
[08:15] Ethan C: Right — it's a trade. Optimize suggests tiny batching windows (<20ms) to capture micro-batches which improve throughput without materially affecting p95. You can apply batching only to background flows and keep interactive routes unbatched.
[08:35] Maya C: Do you have benchmarking templates?
[08:38] Priya N: Yes — we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet and a load test script that exercises streaming paths and simulates 95th/99th percentiles.
[08:50] Sofia R: Recap and proposed plan: we send pricing + cost model, Ethan invites you to sandbox with sample prompts and console recording, you run internal latency test and then we'll schedule infra deep dive focusing on retry behavior and network config.
[09:05] Maya C: Sounds good. Any legal/procurement concerns? Our procurement wants a basic SLA example and data processing addendum.
[09:12] Sofia R: We'll include our SLA and the DPA security pack link in the follow-up.
[09:20] Tanya L: One last thing — offline summarization we might want smaller models to batch overnight. Is that straightforward?
[09:26] Ethan C: Yes — offline or bulk jobs are ideal for quantized variants — big cost savings. Optimize will recommend model/quantization settings based on your workload pattern.
[09:40] Oliver P: Great — thanks everyone.
[09:42] [end of scheduled demo portion, brief social small talk]

Closing (last 2 minutes)
[46:00] Sofia R: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the pricing and sandbox links. Ethan will set up the deep dive. Maya — thanks for the targets, that will help our tail latency tuning.
[46:20] Maya C: Thanks, appreciate the demo.
